data.name: Girinath
data.gender_notes: Girinath is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Girinath is derived from two Sanskrit words: 'giri' meaning 'mountain' and 'nath' meaning 'lord'. It symbolizes strength, stability, and a connection with nature. The name Girinath carries the meaning “Lord of the Mountains” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Girinath usually hope their child will grow to embody lord of the mountains and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.cultural_impact: The name Girinath has a deep rooted cultural significance in Hinduism. Many Hindu deities and revered figures are associated with mountains, which represent a symbol of power, stability, and ancient wisdom. The name Girinath pays homage to this connection with the divine and nature.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name Girinath is believed to bring inner strength and stability. It signifies the belief that the Lord is present in all mountains and that tapping into this energy can provide a deep sense of grounding and connection with the divine. The name is often used as a reminder to seek spiritual growth and strength in the face of challenges. It serves as a daily reminder to connect with the divine, seek inner wisdom, and draw upon the strength of the mountains.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Girinath is a name revered in Hinduism, symbolizing the deep devotion and surrender to Lord Shiva, who is often depicted as the "Lord of the Mountains" or Girisa. The name signifies one's journey towards the ultimate goal of self-realization, under the guidance and blessings of the mountain-dwelling deity.
